analysis.title: Morning Market Tidbits: Market worries go beyond debt issuance
key_insights: Long-end US rates are rallying during the equity selloff. If debt issuance supply fears were the driver, long-end rates would be selling off, so the move points to doubts about whether tech firms can monetize their AI investments.
The equity selloff coincides with rising tensions in the Middle East and concerns around the AI trade, reportedly tied to the need for further debt issuance to finance the investment boom.
French yields rose to their highest level since 2002 and add to the risk-off mood. Social unrest weakens the outlook for fiscal consolidation ahead of the 2027 presidential election.
The risk-off backdrop gives the Fed some cover not to surprise markets at next week's meeting, but BofA says the case for further hikes stays intact unless something breaks.
BofA's 3Q 2026 GDP tracking estimate is unchanged at 3.7% q/q saar after September housing starts, versus BofA's official GDP forecast of 3.5%.
Today's data: Chicago Fed National Activity Index (Sep, consensus -0.10, previous -0.04) and Dallas Fed Texas Manufacturing Outlook Survey (Oct, previous 9.8).

sector_views.rationale: The rally in long-end rates during the selloff signals the market is questioning whether tech firms can monetize their investments, beyond debt issuance concerns.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Tracking is unchanged after September housing starts. It is a mechanical aggregation of incoming data and is distinct from BofA's official forecast.
BofA's published forecast sits below the current tracking estimate of 3.7%.
Consensus for the September reading released today. The previous reading was -0.04.
The prior reading is the baseline for today's October Texas Manufacturing Outlook Survey. No consensus is given.
BofA sees the risk-off mood giving the Fed cover not to surprise markets next week, while the hiking case remains unless something breaks.

Further debt issuance needed to finance the AI investment boom.
French fiscal deterioration and social unrest ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

tension_points.bull_case: The common narrative says the selloff is about debt issuance needed to finance the AI investment boom.
tension_points.bear_case: Long-end rates are rallying instead of selling off, which points to doubts about whether tech firms can monetize their investments, a profitability concern.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Long-end US rates selling off on supply fears would support the debt issuance explanation.

theme_stances.key_argument: Rallying long-end rates during the selloff indicate the market questions tech firms' ability to monetize their investments, not just debt issuance.
theme_stances.evidence: the common narrative doesn’t add up
